newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Peru clinches Malaysia support for APEC admission.
newsitem.headline: Peru clinches Malaysia support for APEC admission.

text.p: Peru President Alberto Fujimori has clinched further support from Malaysia's leaders for Lima's admission into the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, Malaysian officials said on Thursday.
Fujimori, on a three-day visit to Malaysia, held an hour-long discussion with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Thursday morning.
At the meeting, the Malaysian premier told Fujimori that Kuala Lumpur would push for Peru's entry into the 18-member APEC, a Malaysian minister said.
"Dr Mahathir said Malaysia will push for Peru to become a member of APEC," Acting Malaysian Foreign Minister Annuar Musa told a media briefing on the talks between the two leaders.
"Malaysia's stand is that APEC should not be an exclusive club for certain countries as all those in Asia-Pacific have a right to be members, irrespective of economic conditions," Annuar said.

On Wednesday, Malaysia's King Tuanku Ja'afar said Malaysia would support Peru's efforts to join APEC. The group, which comprises members from Asia and North and South America, aims to have regional free trade by 2020.
Fujimori, speaking at a luncheon organised by Malaysian businessmen, said Peru had always sought opportunities to interact with Southeast Asian countries.

"It is evident that on both sides of the Pacific Basin, our peoples have come to foresee the possibilities of an association of interests based on the complementation of our economies," he said in his address to the Malaysian businessmen.

Annuar said Mahathir and Fujimori also agreed that non-economic matters such as labour, human rights and the environment should not be made issues at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore next month.

On bilateral matters, Annuar said the two leaders discussed joint-venture possibilities in forestry, agriculture, trade and tourism. They also signed a general memorandum of understanding on trade cooperation.
Bilateral trade totalled 256.2 million ringgit ($102.5 million) last year, some 88 percent in favour of Peru due to heavy imports of tin ore by Malaysia.
